question: When proving that \(f(x)=x+1\) is increasing, \(f(x_2)-f(x_1)\) equals \(x_2-x_1\). If \(x_2-x_1=5\), what is this difference?
solution:
The output difference equals \(x_2-x_1\), which is positive for every \(x_1<x_2\), so the function is increasing. Substituting the given \(x_2-x_1=5\), the requested difference is
\[
f(x_2)-f(x_1)=5.
\]
